key_concepts.summary: Defense should create a counter, angle, clinch, or reset, not just absorb punches.
Blocks, slips, rolls, pulls, and parries fail if stance and balance are lost.
A counter should be linked to a defined incoming punch, timing window, or opponent error.
Defense should progress from named feeds to random feeds to constrained sparring.
Clinch/reset can stop offense and manage danger but must respect rules.
Any head symptom should stop contact and trigger appropriate medical review.

technical_models.mechanics: Hand, forearm, elbow, or shoulder cover while chin stays down and stance remains stable.
Small hand redirection, usually against straight punches.
Small lateral head/shoulder move with knee bend and eyes on opponent.
Bend knees, move under hook path, rise in stance loaded to counter.
Sway back just outside range with hands up, weight to rear leg, then return.
Glove catches straight shot near chin without collapsing into face.
Briefly smother to stop offense, protect head/arms, then reset on referee break or clean step-out.
Defend, stay balanced, answer immediately or angle out.
technical_models.progression: named response -> random single feed -> two-punch feed -> light spar constraints

tactical_rules.rule: Every defense drill should end with counter, exit, clinch/reset, or tactical pause.
Parries should be small; big swats open the centerline.
Slips should make punches miss by inches, not create huge posture changes.
Rolling should keep eyes and guard available; blind ducking is not acceptable.
Pull counters require accurate range; avoid teaching as a default beginner defense.
Clinch/reset work must include legal break behavior.
Defense-to-counter should progress through controlled feeds before open sparring.

physical_demands.quality: Neck and trunk control during head movement and contact risk.
Knee/hip endurance for slips, rolls, and stance recovery.
Shoulder/scapular endurance for guard and blocks.
Short explosive counter after defensive load.
Upper-body isometric control and breath control in resets.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Late defense increases clean head contact risk.
Excessive slipping/rolling volume can irritate neck or low back if mechanics are poor.
High block/shell volume can fatigue shoulders and guard.
Clinch work can become unsafe or illegal without rules and coach control.
Countering off balance can expose the boxer to return fire.

training_implications.summary: Create defense-counter maps linking incoming punch, defense, counter, and exit.
Assess timing, balance, and counter accuracy, not only whether the punch was avoided.
Contact progression should require demonstrated defense quality.
Head symptoms, dizziness, or visual issues block contact work.
Fatigue should simplify defense tasks and reduce contact intensity.
